sources.role: Primary source for both numeric claims in the draft
checks: By August 2026 employee-directed interactive agent runtime reached six times estimated human work hours. Interactive sessions pool subagents; runtime includes inference and active tool use, excludes waits longer than 30 minutes; human denominator assumes 40 hours/week per employee.
Around 80% of interactive multi-turn session wall-clock time is idle waiting for human input. This has a different denominator from the six-to-one runtime ratio.
Junior technical hires fell from 27% to 9% of technical hires, not a 27-to-9 headcount change. Overall technical hiring grew in absolute terms.
Code commits per engineer increased around fivefold; this is not a direct measure of business value. Adoption was not randomized.
The report describes rising agent-management work and human attention bottlenecks. Its single rapidly growing AI-lab setting limits generalization.

sources.role: Context checked; numeric forecasts omitted from focused Quote commentary
checks: August survey: 10980 US adults, weighted; 1334 staff, unweighted. Job-specific comparisons restrict the US sample to employed respondents.
91% of staff versus 39% of US adults expect Nobel-level discoveries by 2030. These are expectations, not measured AI capability.
A September public follow-up raised the Nobel-level response to 44%; the published main comparisons use August results.

editorial_judgment: The practical recommendations about inspectability, boundaries and selective escalation are commentary inspired by the report, not tested outcomes or claimed personal experience.
media_selection: Native original announcement only. The intermediary has four English charts, no videos; the target has a link card, no video. No decorative visual needed.
live_author_thread_notes: Read the original announcement and five directly relevant continuation posts covering capability expectations, agent hours, output, junior hiring and unemployment expectations. No video in selected material.
additional_metric_qualification: Meta-work 10% to 22% refers to share of interactive Claude sessions classified from 2000 summaries, not measured employee work-hour share; omitted from draft.
